title: Dimension of a binary product of nonempty algebraic schemes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $X,Y$ be nonempty schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For the fibre product over $k$ [def-pc-fibre-product], their Krull dimensions [def-pc-dimension] satisfy $\dim(X\times_kY)=\dim X+\dim Y$.

source.place: Tag 0B2M, lemma-dimension-product-locally-algebraic, clause (2), specialized to nonempty finite-type schemes over a field.

proof.text: Write $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $b:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $P=X\times_kY$, and $p:P\to Y$. Every affine coordinate ring of $X$ is a $k$-vector space, hence flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. The affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] therefore makes $a$ flat. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] to $a$ along $b$ makes $p$ flat. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $p$ and $b\circ p$ are finite type, so in particular $p$ and $b$ are locally of finite type.

source.place: Tag 0B2M, lemma-dimension-product-locally-algebraic, proof of (1), flatness paragraph; Morphisms Tags 01U5, 01U9, 01T3, 01T4

proof.text: Fix $z\in P$ and write $x=\operatorname{pr}_X(z)$, $y=p(z)$. Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to the square obtained by base changing $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ along $b:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its conclusion is $\dim_z(P_y)=\dim_x(X)$: the fibre of $a$ over the unique point is $X$, and the fibre $P_y$ is the base change to $\kappa(y)$. These are dimensions at points, namely the minima of dimensions of open neighbourhoods, not dimensions of local rings [def-kun-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0B2M, proof of (1), equality of fibre dimensions; Morphisms Tag 02FY, lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change (1)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-flat-composite-fibre-dimension-at-point] with $U=P$, intermediate scheme $Y$, final scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and first morphism $p$. Step 1 verified local finite type for both morphisms and flatness at $z$. The fibres over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ identify with $P$ and $Y$ themselves, since $\kappa(*)=k$ and base change along its identity changes nothing [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $\dim_z(P)=\dim_z(P_y)+\dim_y(Y)=\dim_x(X)+\dim_y(Y)$ by step 2.

source.place: Tag 0B2M, proof of (1), application of Morphisms Tag 02JS, lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point-additive

proof.text: Every pair $(x,y)\in X\times Y$ has a lift $z\in P$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], with $D=\kappa(x)$ and field extension $\kappa(y)/k$, makes $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x)\otimes_k\kappa(y)$ faithfully flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] the prime $(0)$ of the field $\kappa(x)$ lifts to a prime of this tensor product. The point correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] produces the desired $z$. Since $X,Y$ are nonempty, this also proves $P$ nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0B2M, deduction of (2) from (1), pair-lifting detail; Schemes Tag 01JT, lemma-points-fibre-product; Algebra Tags 00HI, lemma-flat-base-change, and 00HQ, lemma-ff-rings

proof.text: Use topological Krull dimensions temporarily. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], $d=\dim X$ and $e=\dim Y$ are finite, and they are nonnegative because $X,Y$ contain points. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions], they are the suprema of the point dimensions. These are nonempty sets of nonnegative integers bounded by $d,e$ [def-kun-dimension]; consequently each supremum is attained: otherwise every value would be at most $d-1$ (respectively $e-1$), contradicting the supremum, with the zero case immediate. Choose $x,y$ attaining $d,e$, and lift them by step 4. Step 3 gives $\dim_zP=d+e$, so the same supremum formula gives $\dim P\ge d+e$. Conversely every $w\in P$ has $\dim_wP=\dim_{\operatorname{pr}_X(w)}X+\dim_{p(w)}Y\le d+e$ by step 3. Taking the supremum gives $\dim P\le d+e$. Finally [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] identifies each topological dimension with the supremum of the local-ring dimensions, which is exactly the dimension used in the item [def-pc-dimension]. Thus the required equality follows.

source.place: Tag 0B2M, proof of (2), taking suprema, with finite-type maximum detail; Topology Tag 0B7I, lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions; Properties Tag 04MU, lemma-dimension
